conviction_note: The reported quarter was pre-signalled on 2026-09-16 (NII and fees at the high end of guide) and consensus already sits there, so the print turns on the forward items: capital and buybacks, which lean negative after the 10-year rose another 28bp past the CFO's buyback-pause remark, against mild positive read-throughs from JPM and GS on capital markets and card spend. With a name that fell on 6 of its last 7 prints despite 8 straight EPS beats and peers sold on beats on 10-13, p_up is 45 on an abs move of 3.0, giving -0.3; the findings sum to -0.55 and the two are close by coincidence, not by fitting.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $1.32, revenue $7.99B (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/USB/earnings-forecasts). The company's own guide agrees: on 2026-09-16 the CFO guided Q3 NII to the high end of +4-6% y/y and fees to the high end of +12-14% (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/us-bancorp-at-barclays-conference-fee-growth-and-margin-gains-93CH-4904020). On the Q3 2025 base of $4,251m TE NII and $3,078m noninterest income (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36104/000003610426000039/a2q26earningsrelease.htm), +6% and +14% give about $4,506m + $3,509m = about $8.0B TE. So the consensus sits at the top of the guide. Expenses are guided at +8% on $4,197m, about $4,533m.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 26.7m shares, 1.7% of float, 2.9 days to cover (Equibles, snapshot dated Aug 21, https://equibles.com/stocks/usb/short-interest). A FINRA-based tracker shows 24.8m and 3.4 days at the 2026-07-15 settlement. No September 2026 settlement was found. The short is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism against the negatives. The baseline skew is -1.04 vol points (slightly call-bid, balanced), put/call OI 0.74, event-implied move 3.15%. Run-up is -6.25% over 20d and -0.31% over 5d; the stock is 14.4% off its 52-week high after a record of about $64 in July, so some rate and capital worry is already in the price.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-16 the CFO said buybacks were paused in Q3 because of capital demand (the Amazon card portfolio) and 'higher rates affecting the AFS portfolio', called the pause 'temporary' and put the target at 10% CET1 on a Category II basis, which includes AOCI. After that remark the 10-year Treasury rose from 5.01% (09-16) to 5.29% at quarter-end (09-30), and it has stayed at 5.22-5.31% into October. Over the full quarter it rose from 4.44% (06-30) to 5.29%. USB carried $89.1B of AFS securities and -$7.1B of AOCI at 06-30. A larger AOCI loss pushes the Category II ratio further from 10%, so the call is more likely to delay or shrink the buyback restart than to confirm it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print in the baseline turned on buybacks alone. The stock fell on 6 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 1.59%, worst -5.64% on 2025-01-16), so negative surprises on the forward items have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Rates are public, and the stock is -6.25% over 20d, so part of this is in the price. What the market has not seen is the quarter-end AOCI, the Category II CET1 and a date for the buyback restart. If those were fully priced, the sell side would have cut buyback assumptions publicly, and none of the previews found mention the pause. The latest rating actions found are from July, with targets of $68-75.
findings.independence: The rate path is from FRED DGS10 (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DGS10&cosd=2026-06-25&coed=2026-10-14), and the AFS and AOCI levels are from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36104/000003610426000039/a2q26earningsrelease.htm). These are separate documents. A peer points the same way: Wells Fargo's CET1 fell from 10.3% to 10.0% in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm), although WFC kept buying back $2.5B.

findings.finding: Capital-markets read-through for the BTIG quarter (BTIG closed 2026-06-01, target about $200m of revenue a quarter). JPM's Q3 2026 investment-banking fees rose 14% and equities revenue 49%. Goldman's equities rose 72% and its EPS was $17.01 against about $13 expected. USB's CFO said on 09-16 that fee growth could land 'maybe even above' the high end of 12-14%, depending on deal timing. BTIG is equities-heavy, so a fee print above +14% y/y (above about $3.51B) is more likely than not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat on EPS ($1.35 vs $1.27-1.28) and fees (capital markets +62.5%) with a raised revenue guide, and the stock rose 1.59%. That is the only up move in the last 7 prints. USB has beaten EPS in 8 straight quarters and fell on most of those prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $7.99B already sits at the top of the guide, so only a fee number clearly above +14% is new. The JPM and GS prints came after USB last spoke (09-16). If the market had priced this read-through, USB would have outperformed the bank group on 10-13 and 10-14, and the baseline shows -0.31% over 5d.
findings.independence: Goldman's equities +72% and EPS beat are from a different source (https://startupfortune.com/banks-beat-the-correction-as-citigroup-and-goldman-post-blowout-q3-results/). The CFO's own 'maybe even above' remark is from the 09-16 transcript, which is shared with finding 1.

findings.finding: JPM reported Q3 2026 debit and credit card spend +10% y/y, with momentum in gas and travel. Headline September CPI was 3.7%, so nominal spend is inflated. That supports USB's card revenue (Payments). Management guided merchant processing (Elavon) flat y/y for the next two to three quarters, so the read-through applies to card only.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print isolates payments. On the Q2 call, management flagged slowing merchant processing, especially in Europe, and the stock still rose 1.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy that landed after USB last spoke. Payments is a minority of USB revenue, and the flat merchant line offsets part of it. Most of it sits inside 'payments growth similar to Q2', which was guided on 09-16, so it is small.
findings.independence: The merchant-flat guide is from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-bancorp-sees-strong-quarter-010205551.html (2026-09-17), and it cuts against this finding for the merchant half. The JPM card number is the same document as in finding 2. CPI 3.7% is from https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/14/cpi-inflation-report-september-2026.html.

findings.finding: Peer reaction function, 2026-10-13: the big banks posted strong profits and their shares fell. Wells Fargo closed down about 3% after an EPS beat with a revenue miss. JPM was down about 0.9% despite raising its NII guide. Citi declined (one account says -5.6%). The tape is selling beats into a 10-year at 5.30% and 96% odds of a rate hike before year-end. On its own record, USB fell on 6 of its last 7 prints through 8 straight EPS beats.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a reaction pattern, not a fact. The options market prices the move as balanced (skew -1.04). A market expecting another sold beat would show put skew and a positive lean, and it does not.
findings.independence: Fortune's 2026-10-13 piece has early moves that differ (JPM +0.8%, WFC -1.5%) (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/), so closing moves are partly unverified. USB's own history comes from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Wells Fargo's Q3 2026 release (10-13) shows three pressures that also apply to USB. It cites higher deposit costs from growth in interest-bearing commercial deposits, and its NIM was flat at 2.43%. Its mortgage-banking income was lower. Its provision rose 13% q/q, to $1,029m, and NCOs 11% q/q. USB guided Q3 deposits to outpace loans, with seasonal commercial deposits returning, and its CFO said on the Q2 call 'I don't think we've hit the bottom yet' on problem loans. Against that, USB's NPAs fell steadily from $1,680m to $1,346m through 2026-06 and its NCO ratio was 0.53%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (-1.58%) and Q4 2025 (-0.04%) do not isolate credit. WFC itself fell about 3% on the revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy that landed after USB last spoke. USB's NII guide (high end of +4-6%) already embeds its deposit-cost view as of 09-16, so the transmission is partial.
findings.independence: USB's falling NPA series (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36104/000003610426000039/a2q26earningsrelease.htm) cuts against the credit half, which is why this is sized small. The 'not hit bottom' quote is from https://www.americanbanker.com/news/purchase-of-investment-bank-gave-u-s-bank-a-rapid-boost (2026-07-16).

findings.finding: The Q4 and 2027 NII guide may firm on the higher long end. JPM said on 10-13 that about a quarter of its implied 2027 NII growth comes from the yield curve and the rate increases priced into forwards, and it raised its 2026 NII guide to $106.2B from $105.5B. USB's management sees a 'path' to a 3% NIM in 2027, about 20bp above current levels, and says the curve is the key input. The 10-year at about 5.25-5.30%, against 4.44% at 06-30, raises reinvestment yields on fixed-rate assets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 USB raised its revenue guide (7-9% from 4-6%) and the stock rose 1.59%, its only up print in seven.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 6.25% over 20 days while the long end rose, so the market has been reading higher rates as a negative for USB (AOCI, credit) rather than a positive for NII. A firmer 2027 NII or NIM statement would be new. This is inference from a peer and the curve, not a company number, hence the small size.
findings.independence: The JPM NII guide raise is from https://www.marketscreener.com/news/jpmorgan-chase-co-reports-earnings-results-for-the-third-quarter-and-nine-months-ended-september-ce785dddde81ff2d. Finding 1 runs on the same rate move but on a different line (AOCI and capital rather than NII), so they are two effects, not one counted twice.

findings.finding: The reported quarter is largely pre-announced. On 09-16 management guided NII to the high end of +4-6% y/y, fees to the high end of +12-14% or above, expenses +8%, at least 200bp of full-year operating leverage, and full-year revenue near the top of +7-9%. Consensus ($1.32 EPS, $7.99B revenue) sits at that top. So a line printed at the guide is not news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 8 consecutive EPS beats, and the stock fell on 6 of the last 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It is filed so the judges see that the quarter's headline lines sit inside the company's own mid-quarter update.
findings.independence: This is the same conference as findings 1 and 6 (transcript at https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/us-bancorp-at-barclays-conference-fee-growth-and-margin-gains-93CH-4904020).

findings.finding: The Amazon small-business co-brand card portfolio (taken from American Express, Mastercard network) converted in mid-August 2026. It is described as roughly $1.6B of loans and about $75-85m of revenue a quarter, mostly NII, so Q3 holds about half a quarter of it. It was known when the 07-16 guide was raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print that announced the timing rose 1.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because it sits inside the guide. A first disclosure of balances and early spend on the call is the only new part. The same portfolio also consumed capital, which is part of finding 1.
findings.independence: The tikr summary has the $1.6B and $75-85m figures (https://www.tikr.com/blog/u-s-bancorp-stock-beats-q1-earnings-what-the-amazon-deal-means-for-investors). The capital side is shared with finding 1.

searched_and_found_nothing: Analyst rating or target changes in Sept-Oct 2026: none found. The latest are July 2026 (JPM $69 neutral, RBC $68 outperform, Jefferies $75 buy).
USB 8-Ks since the Q2 print: the EDGAR submissions show only 424B2/424B3 prospectus supplements through 2026-09-17, with no item 2.02, 7.01 or 8.01 surprise found.
Regional peers that have already printed Q3 2026: none before USB. PNC, BAC and MS report the same morning (10-15), and M&T, Truist and Regions on 10-16.
September 2026 short-interest settlement for USB: not found.
Second independent consensus estimate source: tickerleague returned 404, and the TipRanks figure is the peso-denominated MX listing.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Hot September CPI on 2026-10-14 (headline +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y; core +0.3%), with the 10-year at about 5.30% and December hike odds above 96%.
rejected_candidates.detail: Released at 08:30 ET on 10-14, so it is in the window-start close. Its company-level transmission (AOCI and capital, NII outlook, credit) is already carried by findings 1, 6 and 5.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A Stockopedia headline 'US Bancorp falls after Q3 interest income forecast misses estimates'.
rejected_candidates.detail: The story is from 2025, not 2026. The 2026 guide (09-16 transcript) puts Q3 NII at the high end of the range.

rejected_candidates.candidate: J.P. Morgan analyst Vivek Juneja reiterating a Sell with a $50 target on 'October 10'.
rejected_candidates.detail: No year is given, and the price levels belong to an earlier period. JPM's July 2026 action was neutral with a $69 target (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/us-bancorp-nyseusb-stock-price-expected-to-rise-jpmorgan-chase-co-analyst-says-2026-07-29/).

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (-1.04) and the 20-day run-up is -6.25%. My mild negative lean on capital and positioning agrees with the drawdown and the name's 6-of-7 down record, but it gets no support from the option market, so p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 / rule 6 (findings inside the guided range; this name sells its beats): the capital-markets fee read-through went from +0.4 to +0.3 and the card-spend read-through from +0.2 to +0.15. Both sit inside or just above the 09-16 'high end' guide that consensus already reflects.

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission): the capital finding stays at -0.6 because the company itself confirmed the transmission (the CFO tied the buyback pause to AFS rates). The other peer proxies are already sized small and stay filed.
Rule 7: short interest checked (1.7% of float, about 3 days), so no squeeze shrink is needed. The skew is balanced, so there is no sign against a strong skew.
Everything else left standing: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus Benzinga, no finding falls outside the window, and no financing items.
